sections.heading: Copper-Bismuth Bimetallic Microspheres for Selective Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 to Formate
Lin Jia, Hui Yang, Jun Deng, Junmei Chen, Yuan Zhou, Pan Ding, Leigang Li, Na Han* and Yanguang Li*
Institute of Functional Nano & Soft Materials (FUNSOM), Jiangsu Key Laboratory for Carbon-Based Functional Materials and Devices, Soochow University,
sections.text:
Suzhou 215123, China
Cite this paper: Chin. J. Chem. 2019, 37, XXX—XXX. DOI: 10.1002/cjoc.201900XXX
Summary of main observation and conclusion Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction holds great promise for reducing the atmospheric CO2 level and alleviating the energy crisis. High-performance electrocatalysts are often required in order to lower the high overpotential and expedite the sluggish reaction kinetics of CO2 electroreduction. Copper is a promising candidate metal. However, it usually suffers from the issues of poor stability and low product selectivity. In this work, bimetallic Cu-Bi is obtained by reducing the microspherical copper bismuthate (CuBi2O4) for selectively catalyzing the CO2 reduction to formate (HCOO-). The bimetallic Cu-Bi electrocatalyst exhibits high activity and selectivity with the Faradic efficiency over 90% in a wide potential window. A maximum Faradaic efficiency of ~95% is obtained at -0.93 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode. Furthermore, the catalyst shows high stability over 6 h with Faradaic efficiency of ~95%. This study provides an important clue in designing new functional materials for CO2 electroreduction with high activity and selectivity.

sections.heading: Background and Originality Content
sections.text:
Electrochemical reduction of CO2 (CO2RR) powered by renewable electricity is considered as a promising approach to closing the anthropogenic carbon cycle.[1-4] However, energy inefficiency and poor selectivity have prevented CO2RR from becoming a mature and feasible technology.[4-6] In this regard, efficient electrocatalysts are the key to achieving satisfactory CO2RR performance.
[5, 7-14] Up to date, pure metals have been widely investigated as the CO2RR electrocatalyst.
[15-17] Among them, metallic Cu represents the most unique candidate capable of reducing CO2 into valuable C2 and C3 products such as methane, ethylene and ethanol.[18-22] Despite the significant efforts devoted to improving the electrocatalytic performance of Cu such as morphology control, size tuning and defect engineering,[20, 22-23] the practical application of Cu-containing catalysts in the CO2RR is still limited by their poor selectivity and stability.[18-19, 24]
Of note, the main reason for the poor product selectivity is generally attributed to the relatively moderate binding energy of the key intermediates on Cu.[25-27] Many studies suggested that Cu-based materials can be engineered to contain multiple sites that contribute to the binding of key intermediates along the reaction pathway.[27] Based on this principle, the coupling of Cu with a secondary metal could change the binding strength of the intermediates on the catalyst surface and may increase the product selectivity.[28-29] Recent studies have revealed that bimetallic materials may be responsible for the enhanced performances of Cu-M system (M = Sn, In, Pd, Au, Ag) in producing CO, HCOOH or hydrocarbons.[30-34] For example, when Au was alloyed with Cu, the resultant Au-Cu catalysts were reported to show enhanced selectivity and stability for CO formation, which was attributed to the stabilization of *COOH intermediates on compressively strained Au sites.[23] In addition, it was recently found that increasing the thickness of SnO2 shell in
core-shell Cu-SnO2 nanoparticles could tune the HCOO - distribution with a maximum FE of ~90%.[33] These results highlighted the potential of exploring Cu-based bimetallic catalysts to tune catalytic properties and achieve high product selectivity.[35] Bi is a heavy metal with unusually low toxicity. Because of its high hydrogen overpotential, Bi-based materials generally show high selectivity for HCOO- production.[11, 36-37] Considering the unique role of Cu as well as the merit of Bi, we reason that it may be of interest to explore Cu-Bi bimetallic materials by introducing Bi sites onto metal Cu surface or vice versa, which could tune the binding strength of targeted intermediates on the Cu surface and hence result in improved reaction kinetics and product selectivity.
Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of bimetallic Cu-Bi electrocatalyst for CO2RR by in situ electrochemical transformation of CuBi2O4 microspheres. The CuBi2O4 microspheres are first prepared by hydrothermal reaction method via properly controlling the reaction temperature and time. The bimetallic Cu-Bi electrocatalyst shows excellent electrocatalytic performance for reducing CO2 to formate with high Faradaic efficiency, decent current density and impressive stability.

sections.heading: Results and Discussion
sections.text:
Material synthesis and structural characterization.
CuBi2O4 microspheres were prepared via the hydrothermal reaction using the precursors of Cu(NO3)2 and Bi(NO3)3 (see Experimental for more details). Since the hydrothermal temperature and time had significant influences on the product morphology and composition, these two experimental parameters were first carefully explored. It was found that 100 oC and 36 h gave rise to the most uniform CuBi2O4 microspheres as shown in Figure 1a. Polyethylene glycol 400 (PEG 400) was added during the hydrothermal reaction and found to play an important

role in facilitating the formation of the microstructure. To characterize the microstructure of CuBi2O4 microspheres, scanning electron microscope (SEM) imaging was performed. Figure 1a showed uniform CuBi2O4 microspheres prepared under the optimal conditions. These microspheres had an average diameter of about 4 μm. Their surface was not smooth. High-magnification SEM image in Figure 1b showed that the rough surface of the CuBi2O4 microspheres consisted of a large number of nanoparticles. To get more crystalline information and confirm the formation of the CuBi2O4 phase, powdered X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the as-prepared product was collected as shown in Figure 1c. Its diffraction peaks matched well with those of the tetragonal CuBi2O4 (JCPDS no. 01-071-1774), conforming the successful formation of CuBi2O4 microspheres. Furthermore, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis was carried out. The sharp lattice fringes as shown in the high-resolution TEM image revealed the high crystallinity of the CuBi2O4 microspheres (Figure 1d). The lattice distance of 0.26 nm corresponded to the spacing of (130) lattice plane as shown in the XRD pattern. To confirm the valence state of Cu and Bi in the CuBi2O4 microspheres, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was conducted. The peak location as shown in the Bi 4f XPS spectrum in Figure 2b indicated that Bi was in its +3 oxidation state. The binding energy for Cu 2p3/2 and Cu 2p1/2 peaks was analyzed to be 934.7 and 954.7 eV, respectively, which confirmed the +2 valence state of Cu in the CuBi2O4 microspheres. The XPS survey spectrum was shown in Figure S1.

sections.heading: Electrochemical performance.
sections.text:
The electrochemical performance of the bimetallic Cu-Bi
catalyst was investigated in a two-compartment H-type electrochemical cell (see Experimental for more details). The bimetallic Cu-Bi was obtained by reducing the as-synthesized CuBi2O4 microspheres under an applied potential of -1.6 V versus saturated calomel electrode (SCE) for 40 min. The thus reduced catalyst was characterized by SEM and XRD as shown in Figure S2 and Figure S3. The polarization curves of bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst were first acquired in CO2-saturated 0.5 M NaHCO3 electrolyte (Figure 3a). It revealed that the onset potential on bimetallic Cu-Bi was about -0.75 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE, the same hereafter). Beyond the onset potential, the current density continuously increased and reached a high current density of 15 mA cm-2 at -1.05 V. To explore the origin of the high current density, the polarization curve of bimetallic Cu-Bi in N2-saturated 0.5 M NaHCO3 electrolyte was obtained. It was found that the onset potential for bimetallic Cu-Bi in N2-saturated NaHCO3 electrolyte was slightly higher than that in CO2-saturated NaHCO3 electrolyte. Furthermore, the current density was much lower under the same potential than that in CO2-saturated NaHCO3 electrolyte. As a result, it was concluded that the high activity of bimetallic Cu-Bi in CO2-saturated NaHCO3 electrolyte was contributed by CO2RR on bimetallic Cu-Bi.
To identify and quantify the reduction products on bimetallic Cu-Bi in CO2-saturated NaHCO3 electrolyte, electroreduction of CO2 at different potentials was conducted in the potential range of -0.63 V and -1.24 V. During the electrocatalysis at each potential, the gaseous products were vented into a gas chromatograph (GC) system for analysis. It was found that only a small amount of CO converted from CO2 was obtained as shown by its low Faradaic efficiency (< 5%) at each potential (Figure 3b). H2 was also detected as the minor product. As revealed by its potential-dependent Faradaic efficiency curve, the smallest Faradaic efficiency for H2 was located at -0.93 V. After electrocatalysis for ~1 h at each potential, the electrolyte was collected and analyzed by ion chromatograph (IC). The analysis result revealed that formate (HCOO-) was the only liquid product under all the potentials. The potential-dependent Faradaic efficiency curve for HCOO- showed that formate could be produced at relatively low overpotential with high Faradaic efficiency. Impressively, the bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst maintained high Faradaic efficiency over 90% in a wide potential range from -0.83 V to -1.03 V. The excellent electrocatalytic performance of bimetallic Cu-Bi with wide potential window for producing

formate was superior to that of Cu.[16, 17, 36] Furthermore, a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 95% for formate was obtained at -0.93 V. In summary, formate was obtained on bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst as the dominant reduction product with high Faradaic efficiency while minor CO (less than 5.0%) was detected in a wide potential window.
The partial current density curve for formate was then plotted by multiplying the total current density and the Faradaic efficiency for formate at each potential. The partial current density for formate increased with the overpotential and reached a maximum value of 8.2 mA cm-2 at -1.03 V. To evaluate the stability of bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst for CO2 electroreduction, a 6-h durability test was carried out at -0.93 V (Figure 3d). The bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst maintained a stable cathodic current density of about 5 mA cm-2 with no apparent decay. More impressively, the liquid product analysis after the 6-h electrocatalysis showed that average Faradaic efficiency of ~95% was measured for bimetallic Cu-Bi, indicating that the high activity of bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst was retained during the long-term electrocatalysis.
Compared with Cu-based CO2RR electrocatalysts, the bimetallic Cu-Bi exhibited much better performance including higher product selectivity and higher durability.[16, 17, 36, 37] We believe that it was due to the synergistic effect between Cu and Bi, which altered the adsorption properties of key intermediates on Cu-Bi. The superior performance of bimetallic Cu-Bi proved the important role of Bi sites and the bimetallic catalysts in catalyzing CO2 electroreduction. The combination of high product selectivity, large current density for formate and high stability obtained for bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst held great promise for future applications.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text:
In summary, we reported the electrocatalytic CO2 reduction catalyzed by bimetallic Cu-Bi with high activity and selectivity. The bimetallic Cu-Bi electrocatalyst was in situ prepared by reducing the CuBi2O4 microspheres which were synthesized by the facile hydrothermal method. The in situ formed bimetallic Cu-Bi electrocatalyst showed excellent electrocatalytic performance toward reducing CO2 to formate in 0.5 M NaHCO3 electrolyte. High Faradaic efficiency over 90% for formate was maintained in a wide potential range with a maximum Faradaic efficiency of ~95% at -0.93 V and a large HCOO- partial current density of 8.2 mA cm-2 at -1.03 V. Moreover, the bimetallic Cu-Bi catalyst was very stable and maintained high Faradaic efficiencies of ~95% for over 6 h. The superior electrochemical performance of the bimetallic Cu-Bi electrocatalyst rendered it an attractive candidate for CO2 electroreduction.
